sentences.text:
Captioned writ petition is filed seeking following relies;
(i) A writ in the nature of certiorari quashing the impugned communication dated 20.02.2023 in No.605/KANIEM/BRU.KA.VI/SAKANIEM(K) 2022- 23/2214 and dated 03.02.2023 in No.605/KANIEM (V) SAKAEM (V) (KA) BRU.KAVI/HAVERI/2022- 23/2349-52 issued by respondent No.2 vide Annexure-H and J.
(ii) A writ in a nature of mandamus directing the respondent No.1 and 2 to follow due process of law after hearing the petitioners before installing tower over the properties of petitioners bearing plot No.1 and R20 situated at industrial E-state, Savanur measuring 36 x 21 Mtrs approximately to an area of 756 Sq. Mtrs and Plot No.R18 and 19 situated at Industrial Area, Savanur measuring 18 x 42 approximately to an area 756 Sq.trs vide Annexure A and B.
(iii) Issue such other reliefs as this Hon'ble Court deems fit in the circumstances of the case.
2.
The captioned writ petition is filed by the owners of the land in question feeling aggrieved by the action of the respondents in installing high tension electrical tower in the petitioners' land.
3. This matter is moved by the learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.1 & 2.
Learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 & 2 has placed reliance on the judgment rendered by this Court in an unreported order passed in W.P.No.204392/2019 (GM-RES).

He also placed reliance on a judgment rendered by the Division Bench of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, in the case of Shri Vivek Brajendra Singh Vs. State Government of Maharashtra and others in W.P.No.256/2012.

entities.text: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
entities.label: COURT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
4. The grievance of the petitioners is that, respondent Nos.1 & 2 without having recourse to the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, are intending to erect towers in his land and therefore the impugned communications issued by respondent No.2 vide Annexures-H and J are under challenge.
5.
I have perused the communications issued by respondent No.2 vide Annexures-H & J.
On perusal of the said communications, this Court would find that the lines were already drawn in the lands of petitioner.
Therefore respondent Nos.1 & 2 under the said communications notified the petitioners to furnish details for having caused any damage to the property.
These impugned communications are under challenge.
6. The second prayer is mandamus to respondent Nos.1 & 2 to follow due process of law and utilize petitioner's property only after acquiring the property.
7. The second prayer cannot be entertained by this Court.

Respondent Nos.1 & 2 being the authority under Indian Telegraph Act, 1885 ("the Act" for short) are conferred with power under Section 10 either to place or to maintain the telegraph line upon any immovable property.
8. Under Section 10 of the Act, respondent No.1 & 2 are also entitled to enter upon any private property in order to repair a telegraph line and post.
The Indian Telegraph Act, also contemplate a mechanism to resolve dispute under Section 16 of the Act.

Sub clause (4) of Section 16 of the Act,

3 contemplates right to receive compensation by the land owners who are affected by drawing of electric lines or erecting towers.

sentences.text: In the light of discussion made supra, the captioned writ petition is not maintainable.
9. Insofar as writ of certiorari is concerned, no serious prejudice is caused to the petitioner.
Annexures-H & J are the communications calling upon the petitioner to furnish details, if there is any damage to the property.

Therefore, the petitioner is not aggrieved by the communications vide Annexures-H & J.
10.
Insofar as second relief is concerned, the same cannot be entertained as the petitioner has an efficacious remedy under Section 16 (3) & (4) of the Act.
Accordingly writ petition is disposed off.
